verses.zh: 撒母耳死了，以色列众人聚集，为他哀哭，将他葬在拉玛―他自己的坟墓（原文是房屋）里。大卫起身，下到巴兰的旷野。
verses.en: Samuel died, and all Israel assembled and mourned him. They buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David left and went down to the wilderness of Paran.[NOTE:1]
notes: The LXX reads “Maon” here instead of “Paran,” perhaps because the following account of Nabal is said to be in Maon (v. 2). This reading is followed by a number of English versions (e.g., NAB, NIV84, NCV, NLT). The MT, however, reads “Paran,” a location which would parallel this portion of David’s life with that of the nation Israel which also spent time in Paran (Num 10:12). Also, the desert of Paran was on the southern border of Judah’s territory and would be the most isolated location for hiding from Saul (cf. NIV11).

verses.zh: 在玛云有一个人，他的产业在迦密，是一个大富户，有三千绵羊，一千山羊；他正在迦密剪羊毛。
verses.en: There was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. This man was very wealthy;[NOTE:1] he owned 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats. At that time he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
notes: Heb “great.”

verses.zh: 那人名叫拿八，是迦勒族的人；他的妻名叫亚比该，是聪明俊美的妇人。拿八为人刚愎凶恶。
verses.en: The man’s name was Nabal,[NOTE:1] and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was both wise[NOTE:2] and beautiful, but the man was harsh and his deeds were evil. He was a Calebite.
notes: The name נָבָל (Nabal) means “foolish” or “senseless” in Hebrew, and as an adjective the word is used especially of persons who have no perception of ethical or religious claims. It is an apt name for this character, who certainly typifies such behavior.
Heb “good of insight”; KJV “of good understanding”; NAB, NIV, TEV “intelligent”; NRSV “clever.”

verses.zh: 大卫在旷野听见说拿八剪羊毛，
verses.en: When David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep,

verses.zh: 大卫就打发十个仆人，吩咐他们说：「你们上迦密去见拿八，提我的名问他安。
verses.en: he[NOTE:1] sent 10 servants,[NOTE:2] saying to them,[NOTE:3] “Go up to Carmel to see Nabal and give him greetings in my name.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “David”; for stylistic reasons the pronoun has been used in the translation.
Or “young men.”
Heb “and David said to the young men.”
Heb “and inquire concerning him in my name in regard to peace.”

verses.zh: 要对那富户如此说：『愿你平安，愿你家平安，愿你一切所有的都平安。
verses.en: Then you will say to my brother,[NOTE:1] ‘Peace to you and your house! Peace to all that is yours!
notes: The text is difficult here. The MT and most of the early versions support the reading לֶחָי (lekhai, “to life,” or “to the one who lives”). Some of the older English versions (KJV, ASV; cf. NKJV) took the expression to mean “to him who lives (in prosperity),” but this translation requires reading a good deal into the words. While the expression could have the sense of “Long life to you!” (cf. NIV, NJPS) or perhaps “Good luck to you!” this seems somewhat redundant in light of the salutation that follows in the context. The Latin Vulgate has fratribus meis (“to my brothers”), which suggests that Jerome understood the Hebrew word to have an ʾalef that is absent in the MT (i.e., לֶאֱחָי, leʾekhay). Jerome’s plural, however, remains a problem, since in the context David is addressing a single individual, namely Nabal, and not a group. However, it is likely that the Vulgate witnesses to a consonantal Hebrew text that is to be preferred here, especially if the word were to be revocalized as a singular rather than a plural. While it is impossible to be certain about this reading, the present translation essentially follows the Vulgate in reading “my brother” (so also NJB; cf. NAB, RSV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 现在我听说有人为你剪羊毛，你的牧人在迦密的时候和我们在一处，我们没有欺负他们，他们也未曾失落甚么。
verses.en: Now I hear that they are shearing sheep for you. When your shepherds were with us, we neither insulted them nor harmed them the whole time they were in Carmel.

verses.zh: 可以问你的仆人，他们必告诉你。所以愿我的仆人在你眼前蒙恩，因为是在好日子来的。求你随手取点赐与仆人和你儿子大卫。』」
verses.en: Ask your own servants; they can tell you! May my servants find favor in your sight, for we have come[NOTE:1] at the time of a holiday. Please provide us—your servants[NOTE:2] and your son David—with whatever you can spare.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: The translation follows many medieval Hebrew mss in reading בָּאנוּ (baʾnu, “we have come”) rather than the MT’s בָּנוּ (banu, “we have built”).
This refers to the ten servants sent by David.
Heb “whatever your hand will find.”

verses.zh: 大卫的仆人到了，将这话提大卫的名都告诉了拿八，就住了口。
verses.en: So David’s servants went and spoke all these words to Nabal in David’s name. Then they paused.

verses.zh: 拿八回答大卫的仆人说：「大卫是谁？耶西的儿子是谁？近来悖逆主人奔逃的仆人甚多，
verses.en: But Nabal responded to David’s servants, “Who is David, and who is this son of Jesse? This is a time when many servants are breaking away from their masters!

verses.zh: 我岂可将饮食和为我剪羊毛人所宰的肉给我不知道从哪里来的人呢？」
verses.en: Should I take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers and give them to these men? I don’t even know where they came from!”

verses.zh: 大卫的仆人就转身从原路回去，照这话告诉大卫。
verses.en: So David’s servants went on their way. When they had returned, they came and told David[NOTE:1] all these things.
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 大卫向跟随他的人说：「你们各人都要带上刀！」众人就都带上刀，大卫也带上刀。跟随大卫上去的约有四百人，留下二百人看守器具。
verses.en: Then David instructed his men, “Each of you strap on your sword!” So each one strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. About 400 men followed David, while 200 stayed behind with the equipment.

verses.zh: 有拿八的一个仆人告诉拿八的妻亚比该说：「大卫从旷野打发使者来问我主人的安，主人却辱骂他们。
verses.en: But one of the servants told Nabal’s wife Abigail, “David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet[NOTE:1] our lord, but he screamed at them.
notes: Heb “bless.”

verses.zh: 但是那些人待我们甚好；我们在田野与他们来往的时候，没有受他们的欺负，也未曾失落甚么。
verses.en: These men were very good to us. They did not insult us, nor did we sustain any loss during the entire time we were together[NOTE:1] in the field.
notes: Heb “all the days we walked about with them when we were.”

verses.zh: 我们在他们那里牧羊的时候，他们昼夜作我们的保障。
verses.en: Both night and day they were a protective wall for us the entire time we were with them, while we were tending our flocks.

verses.zh: 所以你当筹划，看怎样行才好；不然，祸患定要临到我主人和他全家。他性情凶暴，无人敢与他说话。」
verses.en: Now be aware of this, and see what you can do. For disaster has been planned for our lord and his entire household.[NOTE:1] He is such a wicked person[NOTE:2] that no one tells him anything!”
notes: Heb “all his house” (so ASV, NRSV); NAB, NLT “his whole family.”
Heb “he is a son of worthlessness.”

verses.zh: 亚比该急忙将二百饼，两皮袋酒，五只收拾好了的羊，五细亚烘好了的穗子，一百葡萄饼，二百无花果饼，都驮在驴上，
verses.en: So Abigail quickly took 200 loaves of bread, two containers[NOTE:1] of wine, five prepared sheep, five seahs[NOTE:2] of roasted grain, 100 bunches of raisins, and 200 lumps of pressed figs. She loaded them on donkeys
notes: Heb “skins.”
The seah was a dry measure equal to one-third of an ephah, or not quite eleven quarts.

verses.zh: 对仆人说：「你们前头走，我随着你们去。」这事她却没有告诉丈夫拿八。
verses.en: and said to her servants, “Go on ahead of me. I will come after you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

verses.zh: 亚比该骑着驴，正下山坡，见大卫和跟随他的人从对面下来，亚比该就迎接他们。
verses.en: Riding on her donkey, she went down under cover of the mountain. David and his men were coming down to meet her, and she encountered them.

verses.zh: 大卫曾说：「我在旷野为那人看守所有的，以致他一样不失落，实在是徒然了！他向我以恶报善。
verses.en: Now David had been thinking,[NOTE:1] “In vain I guarded everything that belonged to this man in the wilderness. I didn’t take anything from him. But he has repaid my good with evil.
notes: Heb “said.”

verses.zh: 凡属拿八的男丁，我若留一个到明日早晨，愿　神重重降罚与我！」
verses.en: God will severely punish David,[NOTE:1] if I leave alive until morning even one male[NOTE:2] from all those who belong to him!”
notes: Heb “Thus God will do to the enemies of David and thus he will add.” Most of the Old Greek ms tradition has simply “David,” with no reference to his enemies. In OT imprecations such as the one found in v. 22 it is common for the speaker to direct malediction toward himself as an indication of the seriousness with which he regards the matter at hand. In other words, the speaker invites on himself dire consequences if he fails to fulfill the matter expressed in the oath. However, in the situation alluded to in v. 22 the threat actually does not come to fruition due to the effectiveness of Abigail’s appeal to David on behalf of her husband Nabal. Instead, David is placated through Abigail’s intervention. It therefore seems likely that the reference to “the enemies of David” in the MT of v. 22 is the result of a scribal attempt to deliver David from the implied consequences of this oath. The present translation follows the LXX rather than the MT here.

Heb “one who urinates against a wall” (also in v. 34); KJV “any that pisseth against the wall.” At first this may seem to be a vulgar phrase because it refers to a bodily function and David is angry. But David uses the same phrase when he speaks in a conciliatory way to Abigail in v. 34. There is no clear point to his using a vulgar phrase in that context. Similarly for the narrator in 1 Kgs 16:11 and the Lord’s oracles in 1 Kgs 14:10; 21:21; 2 Kgs 9:8, any rhetorical reason for vulgarity is unclear. The phrase refers to males, is not with certainty crude, and the addition of the phrase “at a wall” does not communicate well in the modern setting. We have chosen to simply use “male” for this phrase.

verses.zh: 亚比该见大卫，便急忙下驴，在大卫面前脸伏于地叩拜，
verses.en: When Abigail saw David, she got down quickly from the donkey, threw herself facedown before David, and bowed to the ground.

verses.zh: 俯伏在大卫的脚前，说：「我主啊，愿这罪归我！求你容婢女向你进言，更求你听婢女的话。
verses.en: Falling at his feet, she said, “My lord, I accept all the guilt! But please let your female servant speak to you! Please listen to the words of your servant!

verses.zh: 我主不要理这坏人拿八，他的性情与他的名相称；他名叫拿八（就是愚顽的意思），他为人果然愚顽。但我主所打发的仆人，婢女并没有看见。
verses.en: My lord should not pay attention to this wicked man Nabal. He simply lives up to his name! His name means ‘fool,’ and he is indeed foolish![NOTE:1] But I, your servant, did not see the servants my lord sent.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and foolishness is with him.”
Heb “my lord’s servants, whom you sent.”

verses.zh: 我主啊，耶和华既然阻止你亲手报仇，取流血的罪，所以我指着永生的耶和华、又敢在你面前起誓说：『愿你的仇敌和谋害你的人都像拿八一样。』
verses.en: “Now, my lord, as surely as the Lord lives and as surely as you live, it is the Lord who has kept you from shedding blood and taking matters into your own hands. Now may your enemies and those who seek to harm my lord be like Nabal.

verses.zh: 如今求你将婢女送来的礼物给跟随你的仆人。
verses.en: Now let this present[NOTE:1] that your servant has brought to my lord be given to the servants who follow[NOTE:2] my lord.
notes: Heb “blessing.”
Heb “are walking at the feet of.”

verses.zh: 求你饶恕婢女的罪过。耶和华必为我主建立坚固的家，因我主为耶和华争战；并且在你平生的日子查不出有甚么过来。
verses.en: Please forgive the sin of your servant, for the Lord will certainly establish a lasting dynasty for my lord, because my lord fights the battles of the Lord. May no evil be found in you all your days!

verses.zh: 虽有人起来追逼你，寻索你的性命，你的性命却在耶和华―你的　神那里蒙保护，如包裹宝器一样；你仇敌的性命，耶和华必抛去，如用机弦甩石一样。
verses.en: When someone sets out to chase you and to take your life, the life of my lord will be wrapped securely in the bag[NOTE:1] of the living by the Lord your God. But he will sling away the lives of your enemies from the sling’s pocket!
notes: Cf. KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV “bundle”; NLT “treasure pouch.”

verses.zh: 我主现在若不亲手报仇流无辜人的血，到了耶和华照所应许你的话赐福与你，立你作以色列的王，那时我主必不致心里不安，觉得良心有亏。耶和华赐福与我主的时候，求你记念婢女。」
verses.en: The Lord will do for my lord everything that he promised you,[NOTE:1] and he will make[NOTE:2] you a leader over Israel.
notes: Heb “according to all which he spoke, the good concerning you.”
Heb “appoint.”

verses.zh: a
verses.en: Your conscience will not be overwhelmed with guilt[NOTE:1] for having poured out innocent blood and for having taken matters into your own hands. When the Lord has granted my lord success,[NOTE:2] please remember your servant.”
notes: Heb “and this will not be for you for staggering and for stumbling of the heart of my lord.”
Heb “and the Lord will do well for my lord.”

verses.zh: 大卫对亚比该说：「耶和华―以色列的　神是应当称颂的，因为他今日使你来迎接我。
verses.en: Then David said to Abigail, “Praised[NOTE:1] be the Lord, the God of Israel, who has sent you this day to meet me!
notes: Heb “blessed” (also in vv. 33, 39).

verses.zh: 你和你的见识也当称赞；因为你今日拦阻我亲手报仇、流人的血。
verses.en: Praised be your good judgment! May you yourself be rewarded[NOTE:1] for having prevented me this day from shedding blood and taking matters into my own hands!
notes: Heb “blessed.”

verses.zh: 我指着阻止我加害于你的耶和华―以色列永生的　神起誓，你若不速速地来迎接我，到明日早晨，凡属拿八的男丁必定不留一个。」
verses.en: Otherwise, as surely as the Lord, the God of Israel, lives—he who has prevented me from harming you—if you had not come so quickly to meet me, by morning’s light not even one male belonging to Nabal would have remained alive!”

verses.zh: 大卫受了亚比该送来的礼物，就对她说：「我听了你的话，准了你的情面，你可以平平安安地回家吧！」
verses.en: Then David took from her hand what she had brought to him. He said to her, “Go back[NOTE:1] to your home in peace. Be assured that I have listened to you[NOTE:2] and responded favorably.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “up.”
Heb “your voice.”
Heb “I have lifted up your face.”

verses.zh: 亚比该到拿八那里，见他在家里设摆筵席，如同王的筵席；拿八快乐大醉。亚比该无论大小事都没有告诉他，就等到次日早晨。
verses.en: When Abigail went back to Nabal, he was holding a banquet in his house like that of the king. Nabal was having a good time[NOTE:1] and was very intoxicated. She told him absolutely nothing[NOTE:2] until morning’s light.
notes: Heb “and the heart of Nabal was good upon him”; NASB, NRSV “Nabal’s heart was merry within him”; NIV “he was in high spirits”; NCV, TEV “was in a good mood”; CEV “was very drunk and feeling good.”
Heb “and she did not tell him a thing, small or large.”

verses.zh: 到了早晨，拿八醒了酒，他的妻将这些事都告诉他，他就魂不附体，身僵如石头一般。
verses.en: In the morning, when Nabal was sober,[NOTE:1] his wife told him about these matters. He had a stroke and was paralyzed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “when the wine had gone out from Nabal.”

Heb “and his heart died within him and he became a stone.” Cf. TEV, NLT “stroke”; CEV “heart attack.” For an alternative interpretation than that presented above, see Marjorie O’Rourke Boyle, “The Law of the Heart: The Death of a Fool (1 Samuel 25),” JBL 120 (2001): 401-27, who argues that a medical diagnosis is not necessary here. Instead, the passage makes a connection between the heart and the law; Nabal dies for his lawlessness.

verses.zh: 过了十天，耶和华击打拿八，他就死了。
verses.en: After about 10 days the Lord struck Nabal down and he died.

verses.zh: 大卫听见拿八死了，就说：「应当称颂耶和华，因他伸了拿八羞辱我的冤，又阻止仆人行恶；也使拿八的恶归到拿八的头上。」于是大卫打发人去，与亚比该说，要娶她为妻。
verses.en: When David heard that Nabal had died, he said, “Praised be the Lord who has vindicated me and avenged the insult that I suffered from Nabal![NOTE:1] The Lord has kept his servant from doing evil, and he has repaid Nabal for his evil deeds.”[NOTE:2] Then David sent word to Abigail and asked her to become his wife.
notes: Heb “who has argued the case of my insult from the hand of Nabal.”
Heb “his servant he has held back from evil, and the evil of Nabal the Lord has turned back on his head.”

verses.zh: 大卫的仆人到了迦密见亚比该，对她说：「大卫打发我们来见你，想要娶你为妻。」
verses.en: So the servants of David went to Abigail at Carmel and said to her, “David has sent us to you to bring you back to be his wife.”

verses.zh: 亚比该就起来，俯伏在地，说：「我情愿作婢女，洗我主仆人的脚。」
verses.en: She arose, bowed her face toward the ground, and said, “Your female servant, like a lowly servant, will wash[NOTE:1] the feet of the servants of my lord.”
notes: Heb “Here is your maidservant, for a lowly servant to wash.”

verses.zh: 亚比该立刻起身，骑上驴，带着五个使女，跟从大卫的使者去了，就作了大卫的妻。
verses.en: Then Abigail quickly went and mounted her donkey, with five of her female servants accompanying her.[NOTE:1] She followed David’s messengers and became his wife.
notes: Heb “going at her feet.”

verses.zh: 大卫先娶了耶斯列人亚希暖，她们二人都作了他的妻。
verses.en: David had also married[NOTE:1] Ahinoam from Jezreel; the two of them became his wives.
notes: Heb “taken.”

verses.zh: 扫罗已将他的女儿米甲，就是大卫的妻，给了迦琳人拉亿的儿子帕提为妻。
verses.en: (Now Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Paltiel son of Laish, who was from Gallim.)
